description: Delete a specific mail message from your inbox server-side. Prerequisite: mail_id is a positive integer; the row in fso_inbox with target_id=<your_persist_id> exists (the server's DELETE is gated on (message_id=? AND target_id=?) so you cannot delete mail addressed to someone else). Effect: sends MailRequest{Type=DELETE, TimestampID=<mail_id>} on the city Aries socket. The field name 'TimestampID' is a serialisation overload — for DELETE it carries the fso_inbox.message_id, not a timestamp. The server executes `DELETE FROM fso_inbox WHERE message_id=? AND target_id=?`. There is NO wire-level response PDU on this path — the only observable effects are the DB row vanishing and subsequent POLL_INBOX responses no longer including it. Cost: zero. Client-side refuse: mail_id <= 0 → ok=false.

args.name: mail_id
args.description: The fso_inbox.message_id of the mail to delete. Returned by poll-inbox as the `id` field of each MessageItem. Must be > 0. Server silently no-ops on mail_ids that don't exist or aren't addressed to you — use a follow-up poll-inbox to verify deletion.

call_signatures: cf $CF delete-mail --mail_id <poll-inbox.messages[].id>                                                   # uses fso_inbox.message_id (NOT a timestamp)
common_mistakes: mail_id is fso_inbox.message_id (from poll-inbox's .id), NOT a timestamp — despite the wire field being called TimestampID.
Deleting another user's mail silently no-ops server-side (WHERE target_id=? gate); use poll-inbox to verify.
perception_hints: Your own persist_id (for self-send health check): perception.avatar.persist_id
Inbound NEW_MAIL pushes surface in perception.recent_events[] with kind=='mail', direction=='in' — the extras carry mail_id / sender_persist_id / subject
Target persist_id: perception.nearby_sims[].persist_id (on-lot) or from your remembered contacts
refuse_conditions: no wire-level response PDU — server silent-drops deletes of non-existent or wrong-target rows; verify via poll-inbox
